summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 27.6% YoY to INR286.2 crores and FY26 posted record INR972.9 crores revenue with INR68.6 crores PAT.
summary.overview: JG Chemicals reported record full-year FY26 revenue (INR972.9 crores), EBITDA (INR97.9 crores) and PAT (INR68.6 crores), with Q4 revenue up 27.6% YoY to INR286.2 crores. Q4 EBITDA of INR26.8 crores implied a margin of about 10.26%, held back by a March spike in raw material (zinc dross) and energy costs. Management said the cost increases were passed on to customers from 1 April 2026, and that inventory gains from the earlier zinc price rise were not visible in Q4 because zinc rose only about 2% between Q3 and Q4. Capacity remains the focus, with the Dahej (Gujarat) plant due for commissioning in H1 FY27 and Naidupeta debottlenecking targeted for December 2026.

segments.name: Zinc oxide
segments.commentary: Utilisation in the late 70s (about 77% per Q&A), with about 10% headroom to 86-87%. Management says over 90 specialised grades offered, up from 80+ at end FY25.

segments.name: Zinc sulphate
segments.commentary: Running at about 60% of installed capacity. FY26 sales were flat YoY, which management attributed to farmers deferring purchases amid rising prices; early signs of demand recovery seen in recent months.

segments.name: Non-rubber applications
segments.commentary: Pharma, ceramics, specialty chemicals, electronics and agriculture. Management said the non-rubber share rose only about 3-4% between FY24 and FY25 and expects larger gains once Dahej starts.

guidance_outlook: Dahej (Gujarat) zinc oxide Phase 1 to commission in H1 FY27; utilisation of about 35-40% in the six operating months of FY27 and 65-70% in FY28.
Naidupeta brownfield debottlenecking expected to be fully complete by December 2026; Naidupeta surplus land available for further expansion, with capacity review next fiscal.
Combined zinc chemical capacity to exceed 115,000 MTPA once both Dahej phases are on stream by 2029 (from about 70,000 MTPA today).

Blended EBITDA margin target of 13-14% with higher value-added products, versus current 10-11%. Dahej expected to add about INR900 crores of sales at full achievable capacity for an INR100 crore investment (funded from internal accruals).

Management expects Q1 FY27 margins to return to the regular 10-11% range as the April price pass-through takes effect; gains from zinc price moves will be retained by the company rather than passed on.
capex_capacity: Dahej greenfield plant (Gujarat): civil works in advanced stages; plant and machinery installation commenced in Q4. Phase 1 zinc oxide commissioning on schedule for H1 FY27.

Naidupeta brownfield debottlenecking for both zinc oxide and zinc sulphate units; expected full completion by December 2026. Management says existing capacity is more than adequate for near-term demand.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 commissioned in FY26; about INR2 crores spent with a payback of 3-3.5 years. Further solar phases planned at Naidupeta and Dahej.
Recycled rubber product: pilot trials done and customer feedback positive; commercial-scale project and adjacent products being worked on. Capex, capacity and timelines not yet disclosed.
Dahej sales mix targeted at roughly equal shares of tire, ceramics (30-35%) and non-rubber excluding ceramics.
demand_pricing: Tire and rubber remain the largest demand pillar; management says tire demand stayed robust through Q4 and into the current quarter. Leading tire majors reported double-digit Q4 FY26 revenue growth.
Industry tire capex announced at over INR20,000 crores over the next three years. Management says customer utilisation is high and the order book for May and June is healthy.
Pricing is LME-linked with a direct pass-through model; bulk of sales are on contract. Raw material and energy cost increases from March were passed on from 1 April 2026, with no undue profit taken.
Zinc dross supply was disrupted by the Middle East conflict (imports froze in March, European shipments delayed). Management says it has fully secured raw material for all customers.
Export share of sales is about 10-15%. Management sees early benefit from the EU and US trade agreements.

Competition: top three to four zinc oxide players hold about 60-67% share, with 30-40 smaller players in the tail. Management says JG is by far the largest in India, and it sees little competition in western India.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation for zinc oxide and zinc sulphate?
qa_highlights.answer: Zinc oxide is about 77%, with headroom to 86-87%. Zinc sulphate is at about 60% of installed capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q3 and Q4 not show inventory gains from rising zinc prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said zinc rose only about 2% between Q3 and Q4. Inventory is rolling under FIFO, and March cost spikes offset any gain, about 150 bps of margin according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Expected utilisation at Gujarat plant?
qa_highlights.answer: About 35-40% over the six operating months of FY27, rising to 65-70% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej revenue potential and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed roughly INR900 crores of sales at full achievable capacity. The sales mix is expected to be about equal across tire, ceramics and non-rubber.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook amid Morbi gas shortages and tire input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Some Morbi ceramic plants are shut on gas shortages, which management called temporary. Tire demand is strong, with June projections in line with April and May, and no price discount requests reported.

risks_watch: Geopolitical conflict and raw material / energy cost volatility, especially for zinc dross and LME-linked pricing; the March cost spike hit margins and pass-through lag is about one quarter.
Dahej commissioning timing (H1 FY27) and ramp-up; management flagged possible start-up losses in FY27.
Ceramic demand in Morbi may stay weak while gas supply is constrained; management expects recovery within five to six months.
Zinc sulphate demand recovery is still early and depends on farmers accepting the new price levels.
Limited disclosure: company does not give volume or product-level realisation figures, and recycled rubber project economics are not yet disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on demand and the Dahej ramp-up, but cautious on the March cost spike and reluctant to disclose volumes, product-level realisations or the recycled rubber project economics. Management repeatedly framed the margin hit as temporary and passed through.
